unsupported_codes.reason: Alcoholic liver disease, the category that holds alcoholic cirrhosis: reporting one treats the cirrhosis as caused by alcohol, and the provider lists cirrhosis and alcohol dependence as separate diagnoses without linking them.

citations.K74.60: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.15, second paragraph: for conditions that the classification does not link by the terms 'with' or 'in', provider documentation must link the conditions in order to code them as related. The inclusion term at K74.60 is 'Cirrhosis (of liver) NOS'. Here the provider documents cirrhosis of liver and, as a separate diagnosis, alcohol dependence, and states no cause for the cirrhosis, so the unspecified cirrhosis code is reported.
citations.F10.20: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section IV.J: all documented conditions that coexist at the time of the visit and require or affect patient care, treatment or management are coded. The title of F10.20 is 'Alcohol dependence, uncomplicated'. Here alcohol dependence is assessed and referred to addiction medicine, and the note records daily drinking with no intoxication and no withdrawal symptoms.

coder_notes: The Alphabetic Index entry 'Cirrhosis' reaches K70.30 only through the subterm 'alcoholic' and has no 'with' entry, and the 'with' list under 'Dependence, alcohol' holds no liver disease (FY2027 Alphabetic Index as released by CMS, read on 2026-11-19; the Index is not among this repository's tracked reference files). The Excludes1 note at K74 sends alcoholic cirrhosis to K70.3, which applies only when the provider documents the cirrhosis as alcoholic. Hepatitis B and C testing is negative and no complication of cirrhosis is documented. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
